The cohort was restricted to tumours with an invasive component over 3.0 mm, which removes exactly the small, mostly intra-ampullary tumours where subtyping is hardest and where the classification would most change management. And in a side experiment within the same paper, two fields from a single tumour shown blind to eight observers were called pancreatobiliary by 6 of 8 and hybrid by 2 of 8 for one field, and intestinal by 4 of 8 and mixed by 4 of 8 for the other. Pure intestinal carcinoma — the phenotype that intestinal-type regimens are chosen for — comprised 13 of 232 cases under the purist scheme, so every statement about the pure intestinal phenotype in that paper rests on 13 patients. The counterweight, which is solid, is that even pancreatobiliary-predominant ampullary carcinoma behaved far better than pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma: median 41 against 15.6 months (P<0.001), and hazard ratio 1.97 (95% CI 1.42–2.72, P<0.001) when matched for size and node status — although that 476-patient comparator cohort is described as previously unpublished, with no inclusion criteria, dates, stage distribution or treatment given.

standard.t: Test every ampullary carcinoma for mismatch-repair deficiency as a reflex, regardless of subtype.
standard.pref: Every case at diagnosis. PERIPAN recommends reflex mismatch-repair testing by immunohistochemistry or PCR, on the grounds that recent studies show deficiency rates comparable to colorectal cancer and independent of subtype, and that deficiency identifies a subset with different behaviour and candidacy for immunotherapy. It asks for the result to follow the diagnosis immediately or accompany the final pathology report. The test is cheap, it is a germline trigger as well as a treatment test, and nothing about it depends on the subtype call being reliable — which is the strongest argument for making it a reflex.
standard.avoid: Do not make it conditional on age, subtype or stage — but do not quote a prevalence figure with more confidence than the data carry. The one-in-six estimate PERIPAN relies on is graded low evidence and is the upper end of a wide range: deficiency was found in 18 of 119 tested non-medullary ampullary carcinomas (15%) in one institutional series, where the 119 were a convenience subset of 348 cases that happened to have been tested, and in only 1 of 23 early-onset ampullary carcinomas (4.3%) in a nationwide Dutch series where the same analysis found 11 of 23 duodenal carcinomas (47.8%) deficient. The claim that every mismatch-repair-deficient ampullary and pancreatic carcinoma in that Dutch series was attributable to Lynch syndrome rests on 1 ampullary and 2 pancreatic patients, and no confidence interval appears anywhere in that paper. Medullary-type ampullary carcinoma, 11 of 359 cases (3%) in one series, was mismatch-repair deficient in 7 of 11 (64%) and should prompt the test on sight.
standard.note: NCCN reaches a narrower position, recommending somatic molecular profiling for patients with metastatic disease who are candidates for anticancer therapy, with microsatellite instability and mismatch-repair deficiency among the alterations sought; the 2021 ESGE ampullary guideline went further in the other direction and recommended against routine immunohistochemistry, PCR and microsatellite instability testing of ampullary biopsies, a position PERIPAN has since reversed. The reflex-for-all position is PERIPAN's and is the live local choice. Whichever is adopted, the local deficiency rate should be measured rather than assumed, because the published range runs from 4% to 15% and no series has established the figure in an unselected, consecutively tested ampullary population. [PAYER]

alt.t: Next-generation sequencing of the tumour, preferably RNA-based for fusions, in a patient who is a candidate for anticancer therapy.
alt.pref: NCCN recommends tumour or somatic profiling by NGS for patients with metastatic disease who are candidates for therapy, to identify actionable alterations including fusions in ALK, NRG1, NTRK, ROS1, FGFR2 and RET, mutations in BRAF, BRCA1/2, KRAS and PALB2, HER2 amplification, microsatellite instability, mismatch-repair deficiency and tumour mutational burden, with HER2 overexpression by immunohistochemistry with or without FISH. Tissue is preferred; cell-free DNA may be considered if tissue testing is not feasible.
alt.avoid: Do not expect the subtype to predict the genomics in an individual patient. A genomic classification of 3,411 periampullary cancers, as summarised by NCCN, found high concordance between histologic subtype and genomic category overall — pancreatobiliary resembling pancreatic adenocarcinoma with frequent KRAS mutation, intestinal resembling colorectal adenocarcinoma with APC and PIK3CA mutations, higher tumour mutational burden and mismatch-repair deficiency — but also significant genomic heterogeneity within each histologic subtype. NCCN adds that the prognostic value of KRAS over histologic subtype is questionable and that the distribution of KRAS across subtypes is unclear because the studies are small.
alt.note: Other reported somatic alterations include APC, TP53, CDKN2A, DPC4, ELF3, PIK3CA, SMAD4 and HER2 amplification, with pathogenic germline BRCA1/2, ATM, RAD50 and MUTYH variants described.

alt.t: Report the rare non-tubular subtypes separately, because they behave differently.
alt.pref: PERIPAN recognises medullary, micropapillary, gastric-type, rhabdoid and osteoclastic carcinomas, and poorly cohesive carcinoma with or without signet-ring cell formation, as entities to be reported separately from tubular adenocarcinomas. Medullary carcinoma was 11 of 359 ampullary carcinomas (3%), a frequency similar to the colon and unlike the pancreas; patients were younger (mean 57 against 65 years, P=0.02) and the invasive component was larger (mean 3.2 against 1.9 cm, P=0.01), while overall size did not differ significantly (3.5 against 2.6 cm, P=0.09).
alt.avoid: Do not fold these into the intestinal/pancreatobiliary dichotomy, and do not carry the prognostic claim. In the medullary series 7 of 11 were mismatch-repair deficient against 18 of 119 tested non-medullary cases (15%, P<0.001), 6 of the 7 with MLH1/PMS2 loss, none carrying BRAF V600E, and 7 of 8 tested expressed PD-L1 by combined positive score and 6 of 8 by tumour proportion score, against 6 of 18 (33%) and 0 of 18 among non-medullary deficient carcinomas — a different therapeutic conversation entirely. But 5-year survival was 53% against 47% (P=0.47), and 53% against 48% against glandular ampullary carcinomas alone (P=0.84), so the suggestion that medullary carcinoma behaves less aggressively is a non-significant 6-point difference. Despite the pushing border, lymphovascular invasion was present in 7 of 11 (64%, identical to non-medullary) and node positivity was 40% against 46%.
alt.note: Downgraded from C to D. Eleven cases with 3 deaths cannot support a survival comparison; no adjuvant treatment data are reported for either group; PD-L1 was assessed in 8 of 11 cases, EBV in 3, INI1 in 8 and MLH1 promoter methylation in 1, with no statement of why the others lacked tissue, which is a real risk of bias in exactly the markers that generate the therapeutic claim; the PD-L1-independent-of-MMR-status finding comes from 4 mismatch-repair-proficient tumours of which 3 stained positive; PD-L1 thresholds had to be extrapolated from lung and gastric cancer because none is established for the ampulla; and medullary morphology was assigned with no blinded review and no interobserver data, against a 50%-non-gland-forming criterion applied retrospectively to slides accrued over 1989 to 2013. The direction is real, the point estimates are fragile, and the authors state that a clinical trial is needed before immunotherapy can be recommended on these findings. Treat the subtype as a reason to test, not as a treatment decision.

avoid.t: Do not let the subtype alone decide whether to give adjuvant therapy.
avoid.pref: Decide on stage, nodal burden, margin and fitness, and treat the subtype as one input among those — see gate 7, where the two halves of the subtype-directed argument are set out.
avoid.avoid: The two subtype-stratified analyses do not carry equal weight, and the full-text read explains their divergence by cohort and method rather than by chance. The positive result comes from 214 resections at 5 European centres, where adjuvant therapy was associated with longer median overall survival in the pancreatobiliary and mixed group (85 against 65 months, P=0.005; multivariable hazard ratio 0.351, 95% CI 0.151–0.851, P=0.015) with no significant benefit in intestinal tumours (115 against 147 months, hazard ratio 0.443, 0.099–1.984, P=0.287) — but in that same cohort the whole-cohort result was negative and numerically inverted, with median overall survival 168 months without adjuvant therapy against 113 months with it, hazard ratio 1.124 (0.756–1.987), P=0.608, and adjuvant therapy was allocated at tumour board on T3/4 stage, node positivity and raised CA 19-9, with no propensity matching, weighting or landmark analysis performed anywhere in the study. The negative result comes from 357 resections at 12 institutions, where adjuvant therapy was propensity-matched on the factors that actually drove its selection — node positivity (odds ratio 5.17, 95% CI 3.01–8.87) and perineural invasion (2.74, 1.59–4.70) — deaths within 90 days were excluded to limit immortal time bias, and the signal disappeared in both subtypes (intestinal hazard ratio 1.21, 0.67–2.16, P=0.53; pancreatobiliary 1.35, 0.66–2.76, P=0.41), at every stage stratum, and whether the analysis was restricted to fluorouracil-based or gemcitabine-based regimens, with no interaction between agent and subtype. NCCN cites a third retrospective study, of 475 patients, that found benefit confined to the intestinal subtype (5-year overall survival 83.7% against 33.2%, P=0.015) — a third direction from a third cohort.
avoid.note: Reid's reproducibility study is the ceiling on all of this: a classification with κ 0.39, full agreement in 23% of cases and 40% of tumours mixed cannot support a treatment interaction, and in that cohort the subtype itself failed multivariable analysis at P=0.39. Neither of the two adjuvant cohorts had central pathology review or immunohistochemistry, and one excluded 369 of 756 screened patients (49%) for unknown subtype — a larger group than the one analysed. Misclassification of that magnitude biases any subtype-by-agent interaction towards the null, which is an argument for reading the negative result cautiously as well; the propensity-matched intervals do not exclude a 25% to 35% relative risk reduction, so what that study establishes is the absence of a large benefit rather than the absence of any. Decide on stage, nodal burden, margin and fitness, and treat the subtype as one input among those — see gate 7.

avoid.t: Do not use the term papillary adenocarcinoma for the invasive component, and do not call pancreatic intraepithelial neoplasia an ampullary precursor.
avoid.pref: PERIPAN's nomenclature: intra-ampullary papillary tubular neoplasm for a precursor growing along the ampullary lumen, adenoma for one on the duodenal surface of the papilla, and the predominant component deciding when both are involved.
avoid.avoid: Both habits move patients between disease categories on a word. PanIN is not an ampullary precursor, and incidental dysplasia in the pancreas or bile duct does not disqualify an ampullary origin.

gates.name: 7 · Adjuvant therapy after resection
crit: Stage II or III resected ampullary adenocarcinoma
Node-positive disease, or a close or positive margin
Medically fit, and within 12 weeks of surgery
Subtype reported on the invasive component, with the mismatch-repair result available
Stage I disease — where observation is an explicit NCCN option
gates.ask: What can I actually tell this patient that adjuvant chemotherapy will do for them, and does the subtype change the regimen or only the conversation?

standard.t: Offer adjuvant chemotherapy for stage II and III disease as a reasonable choice, not as an established benefit — and give both halves of ESPAC-3 when you do.
standard.pref: A fit patient within 12 weeks of resection, with a total systemic-therapy duration of about 6 months. ESPAC-3 periampullary is the only phase III randomised trial to enrol a substantial ampullary population: 434 randomised and 428 analysed from 100 centres in 18 countries, of whom 297 had ampullary, 96 intrapancreatic bile duct and 35 other cancers (10 duodenal, 25 nondescript), allocated to observation (144), bolus fluorouracil with folinic acid (143) or gemcitabine (141). NCCN carries a category 1 designation for fluorouracil–leucovorin and for gemcitabine on the strength of it.
standard.avoid: The primary analysis was negative. Median overall survival was 35.2 months (95% CI 27.2–43.0) with observation against 43.1 months (34.0–56.0) with chemotherapy, hazard ratio 0.86 (95% CI 0.66–1.11), χ²=1.33, P=0.25, and the trial did not meet its primary endpoint. Significance appeared only in the prespecified multivariable analysis adjusting for age, bile duct cancer, poor tumour differentiation and positive lymph nodes: hazard ratio 0.75 (95% CI 0.57–0.98), Wald χ²=4.53, P=0.03, in a model of 415 patients and 236 deaths. By arm, unadjusted, fluorouracil against observation gave 0.95 (0.71–1.28), P=0.74 and gemcitabine 0.77 (0.57–1.05), P=0.10, with a three-group log-rank χ² of 2.96, P=0.23. The trial was open-label, a fifth of the fluorouracil arm (28 of 143) never received a dose, and only about half of each chemotherapy arm completed six cycles. Serious treatment-related adverse events were more frequent with fluorouracil–folinic acid than gemcitabine (70 of 143 patients, 49%, reporting 162 events against 43 of 141, 30%, reporting 81; P=0.002), with grade 3–4 diarrhoea 14% against 4% and stomatitis 11% against 0%. The authors themselves describe the positive multivariable result and the gemcitabine-specific result as hypothesis generating.
standard.note: Downgraded from B to C on the full-text read, and the reason is specific: this page cannot cite ESPAC-3 as establishing adjuvant benefit in ampullary cancer. The trial was powered on 243 deaths and 430 patients to detect a 12 percentage-point absolute gain in 5-year survival (hazard ratio 0.68) across the pooled periampullary population, and the authors state that a separate survival analysis for each tumour type could not be built into the design because the incidence of each would have required an unattainable sample. It was never powered for the ampullary subgroup, and no hypothesis test for ampullary-only survival is reported anywhere in the paper: within the 297 ampullary patients the medians are observation 40.6 months (95% CI 30.6–61.4, 59 deaths), fluorouracil 57.8 months (32.8–84.0, 50 deaths) and gemcitabine 70.8 months (45.3–not estimable, 42 deaths), and they appear without a P value. Two further features of the full text matter. First, the adjustment that turns the result positive was for four variables on two of which the observation arm was prognostically the worst at baseline — poorly differentiated 33% against 22% and 19%, node positive 62% against 60% and 54% — so the shift from 0.86 to 0.75 is partly correcting a randomisation imbalance rather than independently confirming the primary analysis, and its interval only just excludes 1. Second, pooling created a group in which chemotherapy looked harmful: in the 96 intrapancreatic bile duct patients, median survival was 27.2 months (15.4–31.9) with observation against 18.3 (12.9–28.7) with fluorouracil and 19.5 (16.2–36.1) with gemcitabine. Any pooled benefit is therefore carried by the ampullary and other patients, in whom it was never formally tested. Survival differed sharply by tumour type — ampullary 53.1 months (42.3–72.5), other 32.6, bile duct 20.9 (17.0–27.5), χ²=27.75, P<0.001, bile duct hazard ratio 2.13 (1.61–2.83) against ampullary — and the trial's own discussion concedes that intrapancreatic bile duct cancer may need to be treated as a separate entity. Observation-arm survival of 35 months is also far better than the ampullary literature of the era, which implies a fit, early-stage, selected population; screening data on who was excluded and why were not collected. See nonpm for a discrepancy in the extracted guideline text at this point.

standard.t: Choose the regimen by subtype, understanding that every option except fluorouracil and gemcitabine is an extrapolation from another disease.
standard.pref: NCCN's lists. For pancreatobiliary and mixed type: fluorouracil–leucovorin, gemcitabine, capecitabine, capecitabine–gemcitabine, cisplatin–gemcitabine, FOLFOX or CapeOx, and modified FOLFIRINOX. For intestinal type: fluorouracil–leucovorin, gemcitabine, capecitabine, and FOLFOX or CapeOx. Chemotherapy precedes chemoradiation where chemoradiation is being considered for a positive or close margin. Only fluorouracil with folinic acid and single-agent gemcitabine have ever been given to ampullary patients in a randomised adjuvant trial, and that trial was negative on its primary endpoint.
standard.avoid: Name the source of each extrapolation when consenting, and say that the two trials doing most of the work excluded this disease by design. Capecitabine–gemcitabine rests on ESPAC-4, a trial of resected pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma in which nonductal pancreatic tumours were an explicit exclusion criterion: 730 patients analysed, median overall survival 28.0 months (95% CI 23.5–31.5) against 25.5 (22.7–27.9), hazard ratio 0.82 (0.68–0.98), P=0.032 — a 2.5-month median gain whose upper confidence limit almost touches 1, reported early on a monitoring committee's recommendation at 458 of a planned 480 deaths with no alpha adjustment presented, with the benefit concentrated in R0 patients (39.5 against 27.9 months) and essentially no separation in R1 disease (23.7 against 23.0 months), and grade 3–4 adverse events in 226 of 359 patients (63%) against 196 of 366 (54%). Modified FOLFIRINOX rests on PRODIGE-24, also resected pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma with nonductal tumours excluded, and with entry restricted to WHO performance status 0–1, age under 80 and CA 19-9 under 180 U/mL: 493 patients, median disease-free survival 21.6 months (17.7–27.6) against 12.8 (11.7–15.2), hazard ratio 0.58 (0.46–0.73), P<0.001, median overall survival 54.4 against 35.0 months, hazard ratio 0.64 (0.48–0.86), P=0.003, at the cost of grade 3–4 toxicity in 180 of 237 patients (75.9%) against 128 of 242 (52.9%), and with no disease-free survival benefit in the 101 patients aged 70 or over (hazard ratio 0.86, 0.53–1.39). Capecitabine rests on BILCAP in biliary tract cancer, whose own primary analysis was not significant (median overall survival 51.1 against 36.4 months, P=0.097), and on X-ACT in colon cancer for the intestinal subtype; cisplatin–gemcitabine on ABC-02 in advanced biliary tract cancer, which did include ampullary cancers but did not report how many and was not an adjuvant trial (11.7 against 8.1 months, hazard ratio 0.64, 0.52–0.80, P<0.001); and CapeOx on a 31-patient phase II trial in advanced small bowel and ampullary cancers of which 12 were ampullary, again not adjuvant. BILCAP and ABC-02 are cited here from their abstracts and from guideline text only, since neither full text was read for this page.
standard.note: NCCN states that the panel added capecitabine–gemcitabine for pancreatobiliary and mixed type on the basis of clinical expertise and that there are no prospective randomised phase III data supporting these recommendations. The two pancreatic trials are therefore borrowed evidence in the strict sense: both were designed to answer a question in a different tumour with roughly half the resected median survival of ampullary cancer, both excluded nonductal tumours as a matter of protocol, and neither reports a single ampullary patient. Transplanting a regimen with 75.9% grade 3–4 toxicity into a disease with no randomised evidence that any adjuvant chemotherapy helps is a decision about risk tolerance, not an application of trial evidence, and the consent conversation should say so. For stage I disease NCCN offers systemic therapy or observation; observation is a real option, not a concession.

opts.name: Adjuvant therapy directed by subtype
opts.when: NCCN lists different regimens for pancreatobiliary/mixed and intestinal type, so the guideline already uses subtype to choose the drug — but not to choose whether to treat.
opts.pref: The argument for treating pancreatobiliary and mixed tumours preferentially rests on 214 resections at 5 European centres over 1996 to 2017, where adjuvant therapy gave median overall survival of 85 against 65 months in that group (P=0.005) and remained independent on multivariable analysis (hazard ratio 0.351, 95% CI 0.151–0.851, P=0.015), with no significant benefit in intestinal tumours (115 against 147 months, hazard ratio 0.443, 0.099–1.984, P=0.287). Regimens were pancreatic-type, gemcitabine monotherapy in 35 of 75 treated patients (46.6%).
opts.avoid: Read that cohort's whole-cohort result before relying on its subgroup. Across all 214 patients, median overall survival was 168 months without adjuvant therapy against 113 months with it, hazard ratio 1.124 (95% CI 0.756–1.987), P=0.608 — crude survival was 55 months longer in the untreated patients, because the decision to treat was made at multidisciplinary meeting on T3/4 stage, node positivity and raised CA 19-9, and no propensity matching, inverse-probability weighting or landmark analysis was performed anywhere in the study. A protective hazard ratio of 0.351 appearing only after the cohort is cut by subtype, in a dataset whose unstratified signal runs the other way, with no interaction test reported and only 53 treated pancreatobiliary or mixed patients supporting a model that also contains ASA, CEA, T, N, grade and margin, is the pattern of a subgroup artefact. The intestinal point estimate is in the same protective direction and merely imprecise. Subtype itself was not independent in the whole cohort (hazard ratio 1.559, 0.756–3.216, P=0.229); the 16 mixed tumours were pooled with pancreatobiliary after the data were seen; subtype was assigned locally at 5 centres over 21 years with no central review or immunohistochemistry; 20% of treated patients had an unknown regimen and treatment completion and dose intensity were not captured; year of surgery is not adjusted for in any model despite the cohort straddling the introduction of adjuvant gemcitabine; and several reported hazard ratios lie outside their own confidence limits. The whole-cohort median overall survival of 136.5 months is also far outside every other series in this literature, against a median follow-up of 80 months.

opts.name: Adjuvant therapy directed by stage, nodes and margin, ignoring subtype
opts.when: NCCN's algorithm is staged, not subtyped: systemic therapy or observation for stage I, systemic therapy with or without subsequent chemoradiation or observation for stage II, systemic therapy with or without chemoradiation for stage III.
opts.pref: NCCN's algorithm is staged, not subtyped: systemic therapy or observation for stage I, systemic therapy with or without subsequent chemoradiation or observation for stage II, systemic therapy with or without chemoradiation for stage III. The best-adjusted individual-patient analysis sits here too: in 357 resections at 12 institutions, with 81 propensity-matched pairs, adjuvant therapy showed no survival benefit overall (hazard ratio 0.90, 95% CI 0.51–1.56, P=0.69) and none within any stage stratum, while stage drove both treatment and outcome — adjuvant use rose from 17.4% in stage I to 64.0% in stage II and 74.0% in stage III, and median survival fell from 137 to 57 to 45 months. Adding radiotherapy conferred nothing against surgery alone (hazard ratio 0.77, 0.41–1.44, P=0.41) or against chemotherapy alone (1.58, 0.69–2.60, P=0.28), and recurrence was predominantly distant (38 of 58, 65.5%) rather than locoregional (11 of 58, 19.0%). The registry weight points the other way: NCCN's discussion reports that in 4,190 National Cancer Database cases adjuvant chemotherapy gave median overall survival of 47.2 against 35.5 months (hazard ratio 0.82, P<0.01) and adjuvant chemoradiation 38.1 against 31.0 months (0.84, P=0.02), with higher T and N stages appearing to benefit most, and two large meta-analyses of 71 studies with 8,280 patients and of 10 studies with 3,361 report clinical benefit.
opts.avoid: All of the supportive evidence is registry and retrospective, and the confounding runs one way: NCCN records that in the studies finding no effect, adjuvant therapy was more frequently used in patients with more advanced disease. That biases towards finding no benefit in unadjusted analyses and towards finding benefit once stage is adjusted — which is exactly the pattern the literature shows, including inside ESPAC-3 itself. The propensity-matched null is not a clean negative either: matching discarded 195 of 357 patients, the matched intervals do not exclude a 25% to 35% relative risk reduction, half the screened population (369 of 756) was excluded for unknown subtype, matching omitted grade, lymphovascular invasion, margin, CA 19-9 and year of surgery despite grade, lymphovascular invasion and margin all differing between treated and untreated patients, median follow-up of 34 months is shorter than the 57-month median survival, and the 17-year accrual is dominated by gemcitabine monotherapy so it cannot speak to modern multiagent therapy. Black race appeared as one of the strongest predictors of both death (hazard ratio 3.93, 95% CI 1.95–7.93) and treatment omission (odds ratio 0.26, 0.09–0.76), which signals access and socioeconomic confounding that no propensity model built on tumour variables can absorb.

alt.order: Ordered as the published arguments appeared, not by strength — and on the full-text read they are not of equal strength. The honest summary is that one randomised trial exists, its primary analysis was negative, its ampullary subgroup was never powered and was never tested statistically, and the two subtype-directed cohorts that followed differ in method rather than only in result: the positive one gave adjuvant therapy by prognosis at tumour board with no adjustment of any kind and reports a whole-cohort result running the other way, while the negative one propensity-matched on the actual drivers of treatment selection and handled immortal time bias. The methodologically stronger analysis is negative; it is also underpowered to exclude a modest benefit, and the classification on which the whole question depends has an interobserver κ of 0.39. That is the state of the evidence, and the choice below is a governance choice made in its absence.
alt.flagnote: Ratification item: does this programme offer adjuvant chemotherapy to all resected stage II and III patients, as NCCN's algorithm implies, or preferentially to pancreatobiliary and mixed subtypes, as the European cohort suggests? And does it accept a subtype call whose interobserver κ is 0.39, with 40% of tumours mixed and pure intestinal morphology in only 6%, as a basis for that decision? The group should also decide whether it uses the ESPAC-4 and PRODIGE-24 regimens at all in ampullary disease, given that both trials excluded nonductal tumours by protocol. Deciding this in advance stops the subtype being used inconsistently by whoever happens to present the case. Registry: subtype as reported, adjuvant regimen, completion, recurrence site, overall survival.

alt.t: Adjuvant chemoradiation after chemotherapy for a positive or close margin, or for node-positive disease, as a shared decision.
alt.pref: NCCN lists chemoradiation as an option after chemotherapy for stage II and III disease, with capecitabine or fluorouracil concurrent for all subtypes and gemcitabine concurrent for pancreatobiliary type only. NCCN cites a systematic review and meta-analysis of 10 retrospective studies including 3,361 ampullary cancers in which adjuvant chemoradiation reduced the risk of death (hazard ratio 0.75, P=0.01), with the benefit reported as concentrated in node-positive disease — median overall survival 32.1 against 15.7 months (hazard ratio 0.47, P=0.004) in 186 patients with nodal involvement, and improved disease-specific and overall survival in N2 disease in 1,106 patients.
alt.avoid: Do not present it as established. NCCN records contradictory studies on the usefulness of adjuvant chemoradiation in ampullary cancer, all the supporting evidence is retrospective, adjuvant therapy in these series was preferentially given for higher T stage, nodal involvement and close or positive margins, and the one randomised EORTC trial of adjuvant chemoradiation in pancreatic head and periampullary cancers did not report how many patients had ampullary cancer. The one individual-patient analysis in this depot that matched on the drivers of treatment selection found that adding radiotherapy conferred nothing — against surgery alone hazard ratio 0.77 (95% CI 0.41–1.44), P=0.41, and against chemotherapy alone 1.58 (0.69–2.60), P=0.28 — in a disease whose recurrences are distant in roughly two-thirds of cases and locoregional in a fifth. Adjuvant chemoradiation use fell from 20% to 12% between 2004–2005 and 2012–2013 while chemotherapy use rose from 9% to 32%.
alt.note: Chemotherapy first, then chemoradiation, is NCCN's sequence. Downgraded from C to D: every supporting figure is registry or meta-analysed retrospective data with treatment allocated by the prognostic factors being adjusted for, no randomised trial reports an ampullary result, and the best-adjusted cohort analysis is negative. The recommendation stays on the page because NCCN lists it and because a close or positive margin is a real clinical problem with few other answers, but it should be offered as a shared decision in the absence of evidence rather than as a standard of care.

avoid.t: Do not tell a patient that adjuvant chemotherapy has been shown to improve survival in resected ampullary cancer.
avoid.pref: Say what is true: the one randomised trial missed its primary endpoint (hazard ratio 0.86, 95% CI 0.66–1.11, P=0.25), became significant only after adjustment for four prognostic variables on two of which the observation arm was worse at baseline (0.75, 0.57–0.98, P=0.03), was never powered for the ampullary subgroup, and reports no hypothesis test for ampullary-only survival anywhere. Then offer it, because the adjusted estimate and the registry data point the same way and because there is nothing better to offer — but offer it as a reasonable choice rather than as a demonstrated benefit, and record which it was presented as.
avoid.avoid: The overstatement is not hypothetical — the extracted NCCN systemic-therapy page itself states that ESPAC-3 demonstrated significant improvements in disease-free and overall survival with adjuvant gemcitabine or fluorouracil versus observation in resectable ampullary adenocarcinoma, which the published trial does not support, and quotes median survivals of 23.0 and 23.6 months that match the ESPAC-3 pancreatic cohort rather than the periampullary trial. Confirm the wording against the published guideline before quoting it.

avoid.t: Do not start adjuvant therapy without the subtype and mismatch-repair result in hand.
avoid.pref: NCCN asks for adjuvant therapy to start within 12 weeks of surgery if the patient is fit, which leaves time for both results; PERIPAN asks for mismatch-repair testing to accompany the final pathology report.
avoid.avoid: Starting a pancreatobiliary regimen in a tumour that turns out to be intestinal, or missing a mismatch-repair-deficient tumour, is an avoidable error of sequence rather than of judgement.

gates.name: 8 · Locally advanced or metastatic disease
crit: Distant metastases on staging, with biopsy confirmation preferably from a metastatic site
Locally advanced disease, after a second opinion on unresectability
Performance status recorded as ECOG, with biliary drainage and nutrition assessed
Somatic molecular profiling and germline testing done or ordered
Recurrence after resection
gates.ask: What is this patient's performance status honestly, has the biliary tree been drained, and is there a target worth looking for?

standard.t: Biopsy a metastatic site to confirm the diagnosis, using a core biopsy wherever possible so there is tissue for profiling.
standard.pref: NCCN's own sequence for metastatic disease: biopsy confirmation preferably from a metastatic site, with core biopsy recommended if possible to obtain adequate tissue for molecular profiling or other ancillary studies, and histologic subtyping attempted on whichever specimen is obtained.
standard.avoid: Do not accept a cytological aspirate as the end of the diagnostic process when systemic therapy and molecular profiling both depend on the tissue. PERIPAN prefers core material over cytology for the same reason, and asks that the pathologist be told when a patient will not go to surgery so that immunohistochemical and molecular tests are done without delay.
standard.note: In this setting subtyping on the biopsy is appropriate rather than discouraged, because it may influence treatment and no resection specimen is coming.

standard.t: Choose first-line systemic therapy by performance status and presumed subtype, and define performance status the way NCCN does.
standard.pref: NCCN defines good performance status as ECOG 0–1 with good biliary drainage and adequate nutritional intake, intermediate as ECOG 2 and poor as ECOG 3 — so drainage and nutrition are part of the eligibility assessment, not a separate matter. For pancreatobiliary and mixed type with good or intermediate status: albumin-bound paclitaxel–gemcitabine, capecitabine–gemcitabine, cisplatin–gemcitabine, cisplatin–durvalumab–gemcitabine, or FOLFOX; with ECOG 0–1 only, also FOLFIRINOX or modified FOLFIRINOX and NALIRIFOX. For poor performance status, palliative and best supportive care are preferred.
standard.avoid: Do not treat any of these backbones as validated in this disease. ABC-02 randomised 410 patients with locally advanced or metastatic cholangiocarcinoma, gallbladder cancer or ampullary cancer to cisplatin–gemcitabine or gemcitabine, giving median overall survival 11.7 against 8.1 months (hazard ratio 0.64, 95% CI 0.52–0.80, P<0.001) and progression-free survival 8.0 against 5.0 months (P<0.001) — but the number of ampullary patients was not reported, so the ampullary effect size is unknown; that trial is cited here from its abstract and from guideline text only. The FOLFIRINOX and modified FOLFIRINOX options arrive from PRODIGE-24 and the gemcitabine-based ones partly from ESPAC-4, both of which were trials of pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma that excluded nonductal tumours by protocol, and PRODIGE-24 produced grade 3 or 4 toxicity in 75.9% of a population restricted to performance status 0–1 and age under 80. NCCN states that data for systemic therapy in ampullary cancer are very limited and that the recommendations are extrapolated from pancreatic, colorectal and biliary tract cancer.
standard.note: Intestinal-type regimens follow the colorectal pattern and pancreatobiliary regimens the pancreatic and biliary pattern — which is a reasonable inference from the genomic concordance, and still an inference built on a morphological call with an interobserver κ of 0.39. Graded D rather than C because not one of the regimens on these lists has been tested in a trial that reports an ampullary population: the nearest, ABC-02, included ampullary patients without counting them, and the rest excluded nonductal tumours outright. Clinical trial entry should be screened at the same visit, and in this setting that is the strongest single recommendation on the gate. [PROTOCOL]

standard.t: Order somatic profiling and germline testing, and act on mismatch-repair deficiency.
standard.pref: Every metastatic patient who is a candidate for anticancer therapy. NCCN's actionable list includes ALK, NRG1, NTRK, ROS1, FGFR2 and RET fusions, BRAF, BRCA1/2, KRAS and PALB2 mutations, HER2 amplification and overexpression, microsatellite instability, mismatch-repair deficiency and tumour mutational burden, with RNA-based assays preferred for fusions. Mismatch-repair deficiency is the highest-yield single result, reported in 15% of tested non-medullary ampullary carcinomas in one institutional series and in 64% of the rare medullary variant.
standard.avoid: Do not equate the gene with the target, and do not let a negative tissue result end the question — NCCN accepts cell-free DNA testing where tissue testing is not feasible. Do not quote a firm deficiency prevalence either: the 15% figure comes from 18 of 119 cases that happened to have been tested out of 348, and a nationwide series of early-onset disease found deficiency in only 1 of 23 ampullary carcinomas (4.3%), so the published range is wide and the local rate should be measured.
standard.note: A deficient result is also a germline trigger, though the ampullary evidence for that is a single case: in the nationwide early-onset series the one deficient ampullary carcinoma and both deficient pancreatic carcinomas proved to be Lynch syndrome, while the strong signal in that study was in duodenal cancer (11 of 23 deficient, 8 Lynch and 2 constitutional mismatch repair deficiency). Refer on the result, not on the prevalence estimate. [PAYER]

alt.t: Local therapy to liver or lung metastases, or surgery, in selected oligometastatic patients who have responded to systemic therapy.
alt.pref: NCCN lists systemic therapy followed by surgery or other locally directed therapies to liver or lung metastases for select patients with oligometastatic disease and response or stable disease on systemic therapy, after multidisciplinary review.
alt.avoid: There is no comparative evidence in ampullary cancer, and the selection that produces the good outcomes is doing the work. Treat it as a protocol and registry activity rather than a standard offer. [REGISTRY] [PROTOCOL]
alt.note: The liver is the dominant distant site: 38%–65% of distant recurrences in series reporting site, with peritoneum, lung and bone following. Nodal involvement was the sole predictor of liver metastasis in one analysis.

alt.t: Palliative radiotherapy or chemoradiation for symptoms, and palliative care alongside treatment rather than after it.
alt.pref: NCCN offers systemic therapy followed by radiotherapy for palliative indications, and palliative radiotherapy for severe pain refractory to analgesic therapy in the subsequent-therapy setting. Palliative and best supportive care run concurrently in every performance-status band, and are the preferred option in ECOG 3.
alt.avoid: Do not present palliative radiotherapy as disease control. It is symptom-directed here, and the ampullary-specific evidence is confined to small retrospective series.

avoid.t: Do not treat an ampullary tumour as pancreatic cancer because it sits next to the pancreas.
avoid.pref: Record the epicentre, use the subtype to pick a backbone, and quote survival figures from ampullary rather than pancreatic series.
avoid.avoid: Even the worst tubular ampullary group outperforms pancreatic adenocarcinoma substantially — median 41 against 15.6 months matched for size and node status, hazard ratio 1.97 (95% CI 1.42–2.72), and 3-year survival 41% against 11% in the ampullary-ductal subset — so a pancreatic prognosis given to an ampullary patient is wrong in a direction that changes their decisions. Hold the figures loosely: the matched comparison uses a 476-patient pancreatic cohort described as previously unpublished with no inclusion criteria or treatment data, and part of the ampullary advantage in the modern literature comes from the strict epicentre definition having reclassified 21% of previously labelled ampullary cases, mostly pancreatic, out of the group.

avoid.t: Do not start systemic therapy in an undrained, cholestatic patient and call the resulting toxicity a performance-status problem.
avoid.pref: Drain first where drainage is indicated, by ERCP in preference to the percutaneous route, with a stent as short as feasible; NCCN builds drainage and nutrition into its definition of good performance status for exactly this reason.
avoid.avoid: The sequence error is common and it is attributed afterwards to the patient rather than to the plan.

gates.name: 9 · Surveillance, and the familial case
crit: Endoscopic papillectomy or surgical ampullectomy performed — surveillance is mandatory either way
Pancreatoduodenectomy for adenoma — NCCN requires no surveillance
Resected ampullary adenocarcinoma — oncological surveillance for 5 years
Familial adenomatous polyposis, attenuated FAP or MUTYH-associated polyposis
An abnormal-looking ampulla in a polyposis patient, at any Spigelman stage
gates.ask: Who is following this patient, on what interval, for how many years, and who changes the interval when the papilla changes?

standard.t: After endoscopic papillectomy or surgical ampullectomy, perform duodenoscopy with biopsies of the scar and of any abnormal area within the first 3 months, at 6 and 12 months, and yearly thereafter for at least 5 years.
standard.pref: Every patient after either operation. This is ESGE's schedule (strong recommendation, low quality evidence), and the recurrence data support the duration rather than only the opinion: in a 136-patient cohort recurrence occurred at a mean of 3.2 years with a range of 0.5 to 9.75 years, 9 of 20 recurrences (45%) appeared after the first two years of surveillance, and the rate was 5.8 per 100 person-years (95% CI 3.6–8.8), with cumulative recurrence 3.2% at 1 year, 8.9% at 2, 11.3% at 3 and 14.5% at 5 years.
standard.avoid: Do not shorten the programme because the margin was negative. In 22 Japanese centres cumulative recurrence after R0 was 4.9% at 1 year, 11% at 3 years and 13% at 5 years, against 20% and 22% overall, and R0 was achieved in only 416 of 798 specimens (52.1%); recurrence rates in the single-centre cohort did not differ by baseline pathology. The schedule itself, though, is panel judgement: ESGE specifies examinations at 3, 6 and 12 months and then yearly to the month, on low-quality evidence, with no derivation, no interval-cancer analysis and no assessment of cost or patient burden, and the 3-month examination mostly detects residual rather than recurrent disease.
standard.note: At least 5 years is a floor, not a ceiling — recurrences out to nearly 10 years are documented and ESGE's own wording is at least 5 years. Two cautions on the cohort that makes the case for longer follow-up. Its mean follow-up of 2.8 years is shorter than its mean time to recurrence of 3.2 years, so more than half the person-time needed to observe what it describes was never accumulated, and the suggestion of ten-year surveillance rests on one patient recurring at 9.75 years. And its own stratifications run against the usual direction — recurrence in 19.4% after en bloc against 7.0% after piecemeal resection, and 16.5% after an initially complete against 6.1% after an incomplete resection — which is the signature of early residual disease being reclassified out of the recurrence count rather than of a protective effect of piecemeal resection. Whether this programme extends surveillance beyond 5 years is an unresolved local decision, and the honest basis for extending it is that recurrence after R0 is still running at 13% by 5 years, not the single late outlier.

standard.t: After resection of ampullary adenocarcinoma, follow NCCN's oncological schedule, and record that pancreatoduodenectomy for adenoma needs no surveillance.
standard.pref: NCCN: surveillance every 3–6 months for 2 years, then every 6–12 months for up to 5 years as clinically indicated, comprising history and examination, CT chest and CT or MRI of the abdomen and pelvis with contrast, and CEA and/or CA 19-9. Patients who have had an adenoma resected by pancreatoduodenectomy do not need surveillance, because the at-risk mucosa has gone.
standard.avoid: Do not over-read the markers. NCCN records contradictory associations between CEA or CA 19-9 and recurrence or survival in ampullary cancer and concludes that the prognostic utility of these markers remains controversial. A rising marker is a reason to image, not a diagnosis.
standard.note: NCCN's figures: recurrence rates after resection are 28%–55%, with distant recurrence about 80% of events and the liver the commonest site at 38%–65% of distant recurrences. Recurrences are reported as early as under 6 months and as late as 22.5 months, so the front-loaded interval is appropriate.

standard.t: In polyposis, set the surveillance interval on the Spigelman stage and on the appearance of the ampulla, taking whichever is shorter.
standard.pref: Every patient with familial adenomatous polyposis, attenuated FAP or MUTYH-associated polyposis. ESGE in 2019 was the first guideline to build the ampullary appearance into the interval, and BSG adopted it in 2020: 5 years for a normal ampulla, 3 years for adenomatous change under 10 mm and 1 year for adenomatous change of 10 mm or more, applied alongside the Spigelman interval. Start surveillance at 25 for FAP and attenuated FAP and 35 for MUTYH-associated polyposis under the European guidelines, 20–30 and 30–35 under the US ones.
standard.avoid: Do not rely on the Spigelman stage alone. It measures duodenal polyp burden and contains no information about the ampulla, yet about 50% of duodenal cancers in these patients arise in the ampullary region, and neither the Spigelman classification nor its individual components predict the development of ampullary carcinoma. An abnormal-looking ampulla was an independent risk factor for duodenal high-grade dysplasia in one series. The original 1989 paper made the point itself and then left it out of its own score: among the 80 polyposis patients biopsied at both sites, the papilla was adenomatous in 81% against 41% for the peripapillary area, and periampullary biopsy found adenoma in 11 patients whose duodenum was otherwise normal.
standard.note: Downgraded from C to D because neither half of this recommendation has been validated. The Spigelman score was devised in a single cross-sectional screening round of 102 patients, with its four components and their cut-points assigned by expert judgement from known adenoma and cancer risk factors rather than derived from any cancer outcome; no patient in that paper developed duodenal cancer during the study, 11 of 102 (11%) were stage IV, and no formal validation has appeared in the four decades since. Its four components each contribute 1 to 3 points as though equally weighted, its stage boundaries are arbitrary breaks in a 4-to-12-point range, and two of the four require histology, so the modern practice of computing the stage without biopsies does not measure the quantity the score was built from. The ESGE and BSG ampullary intervals of 5, 3 and 1 year carry no citation, no modelling and no stated derivation in the guideline text; they are described there as proposed intervals that seem safe. The stage does still carry information about the duodenum, and the best available support for that is modest: in 77 Japanese familial adenomatous polyposis patients followed a median 8.5 years, high-grade dysplasia arose during surveillance in 5 of 8 Spigelman stage IV patients (63% in the abstract and conclusions, reported as 4 of 8, 50%, in the results and discussion of the same paper) and in none of those at stages 0, II or III, with stage I containing no patients at all. That cohort produced one invasive duodenal carcinoma in total and it was present at the first endoscopy, so it observed essentially no incident cancer; lesions under 10 mm and ampullary tumours under 10 mm were not biopsied by protocol and unbiopsied patients were assigned the minimum histology and dysplasia scores, which pushes them towards the lower stages and concentrates events in stage IV by construction. Refer patients with a duodenal adenoma of 10 mm or more, or an ampullary adenoma of any size, to an expert centre. [EXPERTISE]

alt.t: Compute the Spigelman stage from previous pathology or from optical diagnosis, rather than biopsying duodenal lesions routinely.
alt.pref: ESGE discourages routine biopsies of suspected duodenal lesions in polyposis because they interfere with future optical diagnosis and with endoscopic resection, and recommends determining the Spigelman stage from previous pathology reports or from optical diagnosis when resection is unnecessary because the adenoma is under 10 mm and not suspicious for invasive growth.
alt.avoid: Note the collision with gate 1: in a sporadic ampullary lesion the biopsy is essential and its false-negative rate is the central problem, while in polyposis routine biopsy of duodenal lesions is discouraged and ampullary biopsy carries a pancreatitis risk. These are different populations with different base rates, and the rules should not be swapped.
alt.note: A worked example of the modified approach: one centre stopped biopsying duodenal lesions in 2017, computes the Spigelman score from prior histology, performs endoscopic mucosal resection for duodenal adenomas over 10 mm, and raises the Spigelman stage by one in the presence of an endoscopically evident papillary adenoma. That is a local convention, not a guideline.

alt.t: Endoscopic ampullectomy for a progressive ampullary adenoma in polyposis, understanding the recurrence rate.
alt.pref: An ampullary adenoma of 10 mm or more that is growing, or where invasive growth is suspected, at an expert centre.
alt.avoid: Recurrence after endoscopic ampullectomy in these patients is reported at 19%–58%, residual or recurrent ampullary disease in 15%–38% of patients across cohorts, haemorrhage 4%–21%, pancreatitis 4%–30% and perforation 2%–3% — and there is no long-term evidence that endoscopic therapy reduces cancer risk, delays surgery or improves survival. A Spigelman stage IV patient downstaged by endoscopic therapy remains high risk and in one cohort had a higher rate of subsequent progression than patients with primary progression. Argon plasma coagulation as primary therapy performed poorly, with persistent or recurrent duodenal disease in 12 of 16 patients (75%) and no regression of the primary lesion at 1 year.
alt.note: One Dutch cohort reported duodenal surgery-free survival of 71% at 71 months after endoscopic papillectomy and 74% at 89 months after polypectomy. Maximum follow-up for ampullary disease in these studies was 5.9 years against 10 years for non-ampullary disease, so the ampullary figures are the less mature. All of these numbers reach this page through one narrative review, which collates them as unweighted ranges across 7 cohort studies totalling 181 polyposis patients, six of them single-centre retrospective series of at most 49 subjects, with no protocol, no second reviewer, no risk-of-bias appraisal and no pooling; its own authors conclude that the true effect of endoscopic therapy on prevention of duodenal surgery, cancer and survival cannot be determined and suggest it may be time to reconsider its use. Quote the ranges as a reason to involve the patient in the decision, not as a risk estimate.

avoid.t: Do not substitute a forward-viewing gastroscope without a cap for a proper ampullary examination at surveillance.
avoid.pref: Side-viewing duodenoscopy, or cap-assisted forward-viewing endoscopy, with the duodenum and the ampullary site thoroughly assessed and documented at every examination.
avoid.avoid: Adenomatosis of the ampulla is under-reported in endoscopy documentation even in experienced centres, and until 2019 no guideline said what to do when it was found — so an undocumented papilla is the default failure. Chromoendoscopy is not recommended for duodenal surveillance, and EUS is not routine but may be considered for a large or suspicious periampullary lesion to separate benign from invasive growth.

avoid.t: Do not treat non-attendance as the patient's problem alone.
avoid.pref: Counsel on the expected disease course and optimise sedation, and record a named owner for the surveillance programme.
avoid.avoid: Between 20% and 60% of FAP patients are non-adherent to endoscopic surveillance. Patients naive to sedation during surveillance were substantially more likely to be non-compliant (odds ratio 9.23, 95% CI 1.46–58.23, P<0.05) in one patient-reported study, which makes sedation practice a modifiable determinant of surveillance quality rather than a comfort question.

quickref.title: How likely is carcinoma under an ampullary "adenoma"
quickref.intro: For the conversation where the biopsy says adenoma and the operation has to be chosen anyway.
rows: Malignancy on final pathology 10.3% (3 of 29) — reported elsewhere in the same paper as 11.5%
No. Derived and evaluated in the same 127 patients, all of whom had already had a Whipple; no c-statistic, no calibration plot, no external validation
Biopsy false-negative rate for invasive carcinoma
quickref.foot: Derived in 127 non-familial periampullary adenomas taken to pancreatoduodenectomy at 8 institutions, of whom 59 (46.4%) proved malignant; independent predictors were age 65 or over (odds ratio 3.2, 95% CI 1.3–7.9), bile duct 9 mm or more (3.3, 1.4–10.1), any preoperative symptom (7.7, 2.1–26.8) and high-grade dysplasia (7.5, 2.6–19.8). Use it to structure the conversation, not to quote a probability. The full-text read found three things that limit it. The strata appear with three different sets of numbers in the same paper, shown above. The score was derived and tested in the same cohort, every member of which had already been judged to need a pancreatoduodenectomy, so it is not calibrated for the patient who is choosing between resection and endoscopic management — the authors say the true denominator is unknown and their own earlier single-centre malignancy rate was 29%. And two of the four components, any preoperative symptom and a dilated bile duct, are proxies for biliary obstruction rather than for neoplastic progression; jaundice and stenting were dropped from the model as redundant with symptoms. Lesion size did not predict malignancy (median 2.9 against 3.5 cm, P=0.3, missing in 27 of 127) and EUS appears nowhere in the paper. Read the score in both directions: patients at no or low risk had more major postoperative complications than the intermediate and high-risk groups, though across the three strata the difference was not significant (51.7%, 27.1%, 29.4%, P=0.11) and reached P=0.047 only after the strata were collapsed at a score of 3 and adjusted — and the likeliest explanation is that an unobstructed gland is soft and leaks. Corroborating figures: malignancy in 26.4% of 91 biopsy-proven adenomas after resection, with high-grade dysplasia (odds ratio 6.86, 95% CI 1.58–29.79) and ductal dilatation (11.12, 2.27–54.37) independent, from a paper cited by abstract only; major discrepancy (benign biopsy, malignant resection) in 8 of 35 discordant ampullary biopsy pairs and 8 of the 90 patients with follow-up pathology (8.9%), itself a lower bound because only 36% of patients had follow-up pathology; occult adenocarcinoma in 14 of 44 papillectomies (32%) done for lesions judged benign, after 44.3% of papillectomies had already been excluded for a malignant biopsy or suspicious appearance; and transpapillary forceps biopsy alone 68.7% sensitive for carcinoma, rising to 97% with intraductal ultrasound, also by abstract only. This score is for non-familial disease; in polyposis use the Spigelman table instead, and read its caveats there.

Number of involved nodes matters beyond the N category: in 313 pathologically verified resections, median overall survival was 107.5 months for N0, 40 months for one to two involved nodes and 24.5 months for three or more, with 5-year survival 62%, 31.5% and 30% and adjusted hazard ratios of 1.6 (95% CI 1.1–2.4) and 1.9 (1.1–3.2), P for trend 0.018; median nodes examined was 11 and 45% were node-positive. Two qualifications from the full text. The N0-versus-N1 separation largely disappears once sampling is adequate: in the 150 patients with 12 or more nodes examined, median survival was not reached for N0, 74 months for N1 and 29 months for N2 (P=0.02), 5-year survival 64%, 52% and 38% — so part of the apparent value of substaging reflects understaging in the half of the cohort with fewer than 12 nodes. And adjuvant therapy data were not available in that series at all, so the N1 and N2 hazard ratios are confounded by treatment in an unknown direction. For node yield, a National Cancer Database analysis of 8,127 resections placed the inflection point in the survival hazard at 20 examined nodes and found the log-odds nodal classification most prognostic, but that paper is cited here from its abstract only; PERIPAN, finding no ampullary-specific evidence, defers to the pancreatic minimum (proposals of 11 to 17) and asks that a short count trigger re-examination of the specimen. Under the CAP protocol tumour at or within 1 mm of a margin is a positive margin — NCCN notes this is extrapolated from rectal cancer and that what constitutes an adequate ampullary margin is undefined. ESGE notes that the 8th edition T subcategories are insufficiently precise, with no significant difference in recurrence-free survival between T1b and T2 or between T2 and T3a in two large retrospective evaluations. Grade: G1 well, G2 moderately, G3 poorly differentiated.

Under the biologically honest purist classification there was no difference at all (P=0.65), and pure intestinal morphology — the phenotype that intestinal-type regimens are chosen for — was present in 13 of 232 cases. The cohort was also restricted to tumours with an invasive component over 3.0 mm, which removes the small intra-ampullary lesions where subtyping is hardest, so 23% full agreement is an optimistic ceiling. Definitions to apply when reading the report: subtype is assigned on the invasive component, not the precursor; mixed requires unequivocal intestinal and pancreatobiliary areas with the lesser component at least 30%, a threshold PERIPAN sets without stated derivation; tubular-NOS replaces the old term hybrid where no confident call can be made, with the favoured lineage stated — a renaming that does not address the reproducibility problem, and PERIPAN reports no interobserver study of its new definitions. Immunohistochemistry supports but does not settle it: pancreatobiliary tumours more often express MUC1 and CK7 and less often CDX2, MUC2 and CK20, and the reverse for intestinal, but no marker is entirely specific or sensitive individually or in combination, published studies have used positivity thresholds of 1%, 5%, 10%, 20% and 50%, and the best-known formula still leaves more than a quarter of cases ambiguous. The adjuvant implication is contested but not symmetrically so: 214 resections at 5 European centres found adjuvant therapy improved median overall survival in pancreatobiliary and mixed tumours (85 vs 65 months, P=0.005; multivariable hazard ratio 0.351, 95% CI 0.151–0.851) with no benefit in intestinal tumours, but in that same cohort the whole-cohort result was inverted (168 months without adjuvant therapy vs 113 with it, hazard ratio 1.124, P=0.608), treatment was allocated at tumour board by stage, nodes and CA 19-9, and no adjustment for that selection was performed; 357 resections at 12 institutions, propensity-matched on node positivity and perineural invasion with immortal time bias handled, found no benefit in either subtype (intestinal hazard ratio 1.21, 0.67–2.16; pancreatobiliary 1.35, 0.66–2.76) — though with intervals that do not exclude a 25% to 35% relative risk reduction. A 475-patient series cited by NCCN found benefit confined to the intestinal subtype. PERIPAN's own conclusion is that the prognostic and predictive role of subtype remains unclear because the historical studies used inconsistent definitions of ampullary carcinoma. One clinical pearl that is not contested: the endoscopically subtle, dimple-like ampullary-ductal lesions are mostly pancreatobiliary, while the florid duodenal-surface lesions are mostly intestinal.

quickref.foot: Why the duration after papillectomy is long: recurrence occurred at a mean of 3.2 years with a range of 0.5 to 9.75 years in a 136-patient cohort, with 45% of recurrences after the first two years and a rate of 5.8 per 100 person-years; cumulative recurrence in 22 Japanese centres was 20% at 3 years and 22% at 5 years overall, and still 11% and 13% after R0, with R0 achieved in only 416 of 798 patients (52.1%) and an indeterminate Rx margin in a further 25.8% that behaved like a positive one. The two series define recurrence differently — the Japanese cohort counts any neoplastic tissue including early residual disease, the single-centre cohort requires a prior negative endoscopy — so the rates are not interchangeable, and the single-centre cohort's mean follow-up (2.8 years) is shorter than its own mean time to recurrence. Why the ampullary row exists separately: the Spigelman classification contains no information about the ampulla, yet about 50% of duodenal cancers in polyposis arise there, and neither the Spigelman stage nor its components predict ampullary carcinoma — ESGE in 2019 was the first guideline to act on this, and its 5-, 3- and 1-year ampullary intervals carry no citation, no modelling and no stated derivation in the guideline text. The Spigelman score itself has never been formally validated: it was constructed by expert judgement from a single cross-sectional screening round of 102 patients in which no one developed duodenal cancer, its four components are equally weighted without rationale, its stage boundaries are arbitrary breaks in a 4-to-12-point range, and two of the four require histology that current guidelines discourage obtaining. The stage does predict duodenal high-grade dysplasia, on thin evidence: 5 of 8 stage IV patients (63%, given as 4 of 8 and 50% elsewhere in the same paper) in a 77-patient Japanese cohort and none at stages 0, II or III, with stage I empty, one incident carcinoma in the whole cohort, and unbiopsied small and ampullary lesions scored at floor values so that stage assignment and outcome are not independent. Cumulative duodenal cancer incidence in FAP is quoted as 2%–5% by age 55 rising to 18% by 75, from cohorts spanning decades in which both endoscopic technology and Spigelman scoring changed. Refer any patient with a duodenal adenoma of 10 mm or more, or an ampullary adenoma of any size, to an expert centre. The ACG, ASGE and BSG figures here are as tabulated in the Soons review rather than read from those guidelines directly, and the dysplasia row reflects the original three-tier wording — under two-tier reporting, low grade scores 1 and high grade 3. Verify against the current editions before adopting any single column.
